admin_note: Wyoming is a STATE-ADMINISTERED SNAP program — DFS administers directly through Field Offices, with no county-level policy variation, structurally similar to this roster's Delaware, Nebraska, Connecticut, North Carolina, Ohio, New Jersey, Tennessee, Indiana, Missouri, Maryland, Colorado, South Carolina, Alabama, Louisiana, Kentucky, Oklahoma, Utah, Iowa, Arkansas, Mississippi, Kansas, and New Mexico packs. GENUINE STRUCTURAL FLAGSHIP FINDING: Wyoming is one of a minority of only 9 states nationally that does NOT run Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility (BBCE) — confirmed independently by both USDA FNS's own 16th-edition SNAP State Options Report (June 2024, Wyoming listed under 'No BBCE (9)') and Wyoming's own DFS SNAP and POWER Policy Manual Section 502, which defines categorical eligibility narrowly as SSI/POWER/Tribal-TANF recipiency only, with no 200% FPL gross-income gate anywhere in the manual or in DFS's own published income-limit table. SECOND FLAGSHIP FINDING, a primary-source CORRECTION of a stale, template-style secondary-source claim this pack found repeated across several low-quality aggregator sites describing Wyoming as having a 'modified' drug-felony SNAP ban conditioned on sentence/treatment compliance: this pack fetched USDA FNS's own 16th-edition State Options Report directly and found Wyoming listed under 'No disqualification (28)' for the Drug Felony Disqualifications option, independently corroborated by the complete absence of any drug-felony-conviction disqualification section anywhere in DFS's own SNAP and POWER Policy Manual Section 600 series (which runs 601-610 covering age through fleeing-felon/probation-violator status, with no drug-felony section at all). Wyoming has FULLY opted out of the federal drug-felony SNAP ban, not modified it. THIRD FINDING (tribal land / FDPIR, specifically researched per this pack's scope): Wyoming's DFS manual explicitly lists 'is a member of an Indian tribe' as one of only seven categorical exemptions from the ABAWD (able-bodied adult without dependents) work-requirement time limit (Section 708(B)(7)) — relevant given the significant population of the Wind River Reservation (shared by the Eastern Shoshone and Northern Arapaho tribes) within Wyoming. Separately, DFS's manual (Section 402) confirms SNAP and the Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations (FDPIR) are mutually exclusive: a household must choose one or the other, and 'under no circumstances shall any household participate simultaneously' in both. DFS's manual also directs enrolled Tribal members resident in Fremont or Hot Springs County (the two counties overlapping Wind River) applying for Tribal TANF to have that application processed at the appropriate Tribal TANF office. This pack found no DFS-published SNAP-specific administrative carve-out beyond these three points and discloses that scope explicitly rather than assuming either a broader or narrower tribal-administration structure exists.
system: Wyoming DFS processes SNAP centrally through DFS Field Offices (no county offices with independent policy authority); Wyoming uses a PAPER application only (DFS 100 / DFS 100S Spanish) submitted in person, by mail, fax, or email to snappowerservice@wyo.gov — this pack found no online self-service SNAP application portal for Wyoming, a genuine structural contrast with most other states in this roster. Wyoming's standard SNAP certification period is capped at 12 months for ALL households, including all-elderly/disabled households with no earned income — Wyoming does NOT extend to a 24-month certification period the way several other states in this roster do (per DFS Manual Section 1201(J), effective January 1, 2016). Wyoming's own DFS manual is unusually current: its ABAWD section (708) already reflects the post-OBBBA age band (18-64 as of the OBBBA's July 4, 2025 effective date) and its citizenship section (606) already reflects the OBBBA noncitizen-eligibility restructuring, both with direct links to FNS implementation guidance embedded in the manual text itself — a notable contrast with this roster's Delaware pack, whose manual was found lagging DHSS's live consumer pages in multiple places.
